newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee head - premature to give restart date.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee head - premature to give restart date.

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear power plant president said Thursday it was too soon to say when the troubled plant would restart or how much it will cost.

Officials said they hope to obtain replacements for 68 faulty fuel assembles by early summer, but also need to inspect the steam generator and address operational problems cited by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).

"All those put together, it would be premature for me at this point in time to say were going to get everything done in the same time frame that we obtain the new fuel," the new president Mike Sellman told reporters.
NRC said earlier Thursday in its daily plant status report that Maine Yankee, in Wiscasset, Maine, could restart in August following the fuel bundle replacement.
"It will take us until early summer just to get the fuel assemblies. There are a number of issues that will affect restart and fuel is one," Sellman said.
The 910-megawatt facility has been off line since Dec 6, 1996. It was shut down to fix misrouted electrical cables, but officials later decided they also needed to replace leaking fuel rods.
Sellman said the plant was developing an "integrated start-up plan," and hoped to have an estimate on how much it will cost "in a few weeks." The restart plan will have to be approved by NRC.

Maine Yankee pledged in December to spend $38 million in 1997 to address equipment and safety problems cited by the NRC -- which has placed the plant on its Watch List of nuclear facilities needing closer inspection.

Sellman said the steam generator inspection will examine sections of tubes that were not "resleaved" in a $24 million repair project in 1995. The repairs corrected a problem with cracks, and the inspection will examine if additional cracking has developed.
In addition to replacing the 68 faulty fuel assemblies, Maine Yankee officials said they will replace 24 assemblies that had been scheduled to get new radioactive fuel in the fall of 1997.

Sellman, 49, a veteran plant manager, took his post as head of the plant this week. He remains an employee of Entergy Nuclear Inc which Thursday signed a contract to manage the troubled 24-year-old facility until Sept 30.
Maine Yankee and Entergy are negotiating a "longer term" contract that would include performance incentives. The 24-year-old plant is currently lincensed to operate until the year 2008.
"I would assume that if we do what we intend to do, which is run the plant safely and reliably, we will be here for the duration," Sellman said.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
